svg.title: What a Double Close Costs Versus an Assignment
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-assign-vs-double-close-costs; chapter number: 2; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: What a Double Close Costs Versus an Assignment; subtitle: Funding fees, closing hits and the spread where operators switch; caption: Assignment is the cheap default exit; operators switch to a double close only when the spread is fat enough to absorb two closings and a funding fee.; assumptions note: Where no single figure was cited, the typical marker is the range midpoint. The switch point spans Lex Levinrad at $10,000, Brent Daniels at $15,000 and Jamil Damji at $20,000.; note: Attributed to Michael (The Virtual Investor), Brent Daniels (Wholesaling Inc), David Olds REI, Jamil Damji and Lex Levinrad.; unit: USD; bars: label: Funding fee on a $100,000 loan; min: 1000; max: 3000; typical: 2000; display: $1,000-$3,000 (1% to 3%); label: Flat transactional funding quotes; min: 1500; max: 5000; typical: 3250; display: $1,500-$5,000 flat; label: Purchase-side closing cost hit; min: 2500; max: 4000; typical: 3250; display: $2,500-$4,000 plus 1%-2% origination; label: Profit lost to title on a double close; min: 6000; max: 7000; typical: 6000; display: $14,000 net vs $20,000 assigned; label: Double-close switch point; min: 10000; max: 20000; typical: 15000; display: $10,000-$20,000 spread
